tasks.short: Prepare approved records for certified postal dispatch and retain proof of posting.

steps.what: Retrieve approved records and dispatch instructions from the {DOCS}.
Check recipient details in the {CRM} and confirm the required postal service.
Prepare an enclosure list and dispatch cover sheet in the {DOCS}.
Print and collate records using {OTHER} office printing equipment.
Book the postal service and produce labels in the {OTHER} postal shipping system.
Check enclosures, pack records, and attach the postal label.
Hand the released mailing to the postal carrier and obtain a posting receipt.
File the posting receipt and tracking number against the case in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: A configured flow retrieves approved records from the {DOCS} and recipient details from the {CRM}; deterministic code generates the print packet and enclosure list. After the clerk approves service and cost, an integration books dispatch in the {OTHER} postal shipping system and links its tracking number to the case. People print, pack and release the mailing; configured filing in the {DOCS} links electronic receipts and leaves paper receipt capture to the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handling remains necessary. Repeated address entry, document assembly and receipt filing sit across separate systems, making a small, infrequent task expensive to connect.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building packet templates and narrow integrations. Existing validation rules and filing workflows handle the structured work without a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: The accepted postal service and required evidence depend on the document and national rules. Physical enclosure checks remain necessary, and postal interfaces may be limited. GDPR access and retention requirements still apply.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk resolves conflicting addresses, recognises unusual dispatch instructions and checks that the physical envelope contains the intended records.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling packets and retyping tracking details, but still handles physical checks and exceptions. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Answer a customer's request for proof that correspondence was posted.
reach.learn: Locate dispatch evidence and distinguish proof of posting from proof of delivery.

evidence.claim: Physical printing, packing and postal handover remain manual in this design; time shares are planning estimates.
Rossum documents structured data checks, exception routing and record posting; this is analogous evidence, not proof of postal integration.
Packet generation, label requests and receipt linking can use deterministic rules when identifiers and interfaces are available.
GDPR requires appropriate access controls and retention limits for personal information in dispatch records.

assumptions: The records have already received substantive approval before this task starts.
A correspondence clerk prepares the mailing and a mailroom assistant handles carrier handover.
Recipient details are held in the {CRM}; approved records are held in the {DOCS}.
The design retains physical certified dispatch.
Build ranges cover one document repository and one postal connection, excluding postage and major equipment changes.
The access range includes an initial consultation assessment; any formal employee consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which postal service provides legally sufficient evidence for each document category?
Can the {OTHER} postal shipping system accept structured bookings and return tracking identifiers?
Are posting receipts electronic, paper, or both?
Who may approve postage costs and release confidential records?
Which retention periods and repository permissions apply?
Does the change require employee consultation under applicable national rules?
How many mailings and exceptional dispatch instructions occur each month?
research_questions: Can configuration of the existing {DOCS} replace custom packet generation?
Does the postal interface support duplicate-booking protection and receipt retrieval?
Can barcode-based filing reliably link paper receipts to the correct case?
new_work: Review flagged address conflicts and postal service exceptions.
Capture paper receipts and resolve unmatched dispatch evidence.
Maintain packet templates, service rules and repository mappings.
Handle failed bookings, duplicate-label attempts and integration failures.

role.altitude: Less preparation and filing work leaves more time for correspondence exceptions. Physical dispatch responsibilities and approval rights remain unchanged.
reach: Support customer service representatives with reliable dispatch evidence.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a dependable dispatch evidence service that helps customer support resolve disputes about whether correspondence was posted.
